33 A student sets up a circuit. The circuit diagram shows how the positive and negative terminals of
a voltmeter are connected to the circuit. The voltmeter has an initial reading that is positive.
V
+
–
Which changes, if any, in temperature and light intensity would cause the voltmeter reading to
decrease?
temperature
light intensity
A
increase
increase
B
no change
decrease
C
decrease
no change
D
decrease
decrease

hints: Notice the voltmeter + lead is on the thermistor divider and the - lead is on the LDR divider, so the reading is $V_{left}-V_{right}$ and it starts positive.
Recall how an NTC thermistor responds to temperature rise and how an LDR responds to light intensity rise, then apply the potential divider rule to each middle point.
Check whether a fall in $V_{left}$ or a rise in $V_{right}$ makes the difference smaller, and match this to the temperature and light changes.
walkthrough: Identify the two dividers: left middle potential $V_{left}$ is set by the top fixed resistor and bottom thermistor, right middle potential $V_{right}$ is set by the top LDR and bottom fixed resistor.
Use $V_{out}=V_{s} \times R_{bottom}/(R_{top}+R_{bottom})$ for each side measured from the bottom rail, so $V_{left}=V_{s}R_{therm}/(R_{1}+R_{therm})$ and $V_{right}=V_{s}R_{2}/(R_{LDR}+R_{2})$.
The meter reads $V_{left}-V_{right}$ because + is on the left and - is on the right, and this is initially positive so $V_{left} > V_{right}$.

An increase in temperature decreases NTC thermistor resistance, so $R_{therm}$ falls and $V_{left}$ falls. An increase in light intensity decreases LDR resistance, so the denominator $R_{LDR}+R_{2}$ falls and $V_{right}$ rises.
A smaller $V_{left}$ minus a larger $V_{right}$ gives a smaller positive difference, so the voltmeter reading decreases. This is option A.

A.explanation: Higher temperature lowers the thermistor resistance so $V_{left}$ falls, and higher light intensity lowers the LDR resistance so $V_{right}$ rises, so $V_{left}-V_{right}$ decreases.

B.explanation: Lower light intensity raises LDR resistance so $V_{right}$ falls, which increases $V_{left}-V_{right}$ rather than decreasing it.

C.explanation: Lower temperature raises thermistor resistance so $V_{left}$ rises, which increases $V_{left}-V_{right}$ rather than decreasing it.

D.explanation: Both lower temperature and lower light intensity raise the sensor resistances, raising $V_{left}$ and lowering $V_{right}$, so the difference increases.
